newsitem.title: UK: LME markets ease at close as copper trims gains.
newsitem.headline: LME markets ease at close as copper trims gains.

text.p: Copper prices tumbled back from midsession three-week peaks during lively Friday afternoon LME trading, as the earlier highs near $1,990 proved too tempting and encouraged widespread profit-taking, traders said.

Also, there was less concern that an option-related spike was on the cards, and with the backwardation similarly relaxing the market spiralled back under the key $1,970 chart level, but still closed steadier.
"Basically, it got carried away by the stocks (decline) and did a little bit too much too soon. It still favours the upside as stocks are going down further," one trader said.
Inventories dropped by 9,300 tonnes, much as expected, but still making the drawdowns for the week some 18,000 tonnes. Total stocks are now at 247,325 tonnes.

Meanwhile, the cash/threes spread touched $8 backwardation at one point today when trade short-covering and speculative stops triggered above $1,970 were in full flow. However, by the close this key rate was back at level money.
In the short-term the market will remain volatile ahead of Wednesday's October options declarations, as there is significant open interest at the $2,000 strike.
Last business was at $1,957 a tonne, still up $13 from Thursday's kerb close. Elsewhere in the metals complex prices tacked lower this afternoon, matching the copper trend, traders said.

Aluminium trading was erratic during the late kerb, as the market briefly threatened to decline under the $1,400 level once more when some stops were initiated down to $1,405. But enough support emerged to stem this decline, and last trade was at $1,409, still down $7.

Traders said the market appears to have limited upside potential unless there are further sharp advances in copper. Given that inventories are rising remorselessly, with another 4,050 tonnes delivered into warehouses today, prices will struggle near $1,420.
Nickel prices tumbled lower during afternoon ring and kerb trading, against a background of news that Inco had reached a tentative agreement at its Manitoba facilities.
"It does not have a lot going for it at the moment, although the Inco news was not really a factor - the market has not paid too much attention to this all the way through," a trader said.

Meanwhile, stocks continue to climb, with inventories rising another 624 tonnes today. Three months prices sagged back to the $7,200 level at one stage before ending at $7,210, down $130 from Thursday.
Other metals fluctuated with the general trend with lead ending at $778, down $4, zinc at $1,024, up $2, tin at $6,070 down $25 and alloy at $1,245/$1,250, up $20 a tonne.
